title: IT Q2 Preview: Large Caps May Cut Guidance as AI Deflation Hits 7%
excerpt: ICICI Securities and Kotak expect Infosys to cut FY27 guidance to 1.5-2.5% as AI concessions bite; mid-caps like Persistent and Coforge are set to outgrow the majors again.
body:
• ICICI Securities expects Infosys to cut its FY27 constant-currency revenue guidance to 1.5-2.5% from 1.5-3.0%; Kotak concurs, while Citi is more cautious at 1-2% — and HCLTech is expected to narrow its growth band to 2-3% from 1-4%.
  • Kotak estimates AI-led productivity concessions are running at roughly 7% gross and 3.5% net deflation, now visible in the base business, as AI efficiency gains are passed back to clients and open-weight models intensify pricing pressure.
  • Mid-cap firms are expected to buck the trend again: Kotak forecasts Persistent Systems at 7% quarter-on-quarter constant-currency growth, Coforge at 4.5% and Mphasis at 3.5%, against 0.5-2% for the large caps.
  • TCS opens the results season first, with Infosys reporting Q2 FY27 on October 22-23; investors watching for margin stability, where rupee depreciation of 8.4% year-on-year has partly offset pricing pressure.

Guidance Cuts on the Table

The September quarter was supposed to be seasonally strong for India's IT majors. Brokerages say it will be anything but. ICICI Securities expects Infosys to trim its FY27 constant-currency revenue guidance to 1.5-2.5%, down from 1.5-3.0% — with acquisitions contributing 1.7 percentage points of growth on their own, the organic number looks thinner still. Kotak Institutional Equities reaches the same conclusion; Citi goes further, pencilling in just 1-2%.

HCLTech is expected to narrow its full-year growth band to 2-3% from 1-4%, while Wipro is seen guiding third-quarter revenue flat to 2% down sequentially. For ET consensus, TCS is forecast at 0.5% quarter-on-quarter and 2.8% year-on-year organic growth, Infosys at 1.1% quarter-on-quarter and barely 0.2% year-on-year.

"We expect muted growth for tier 1 IT companies in a seasonally strong quarter. AI deflation and, to a lesser extent, weaker macro will contribute to weak growth."

— Kotak Institutional Equities

What AI Deflation Means in Numbers

"AI deflation" is no longer an analyst catchphrase — it now has a price. Kotak estimates gross deflation of around 7% and net deflation of 3.5% as AI-driven productivity gains are conceded to clients in continuous pricing resets, now visible in the base business rather than just new deals. The spread of open-source and open-weight models is intensifying the pressure.

HDFC Securities adds that new AI-centric deal wins are only partly offsetting the expected 6-7% deflation impact, and conversion into revenue remains slow — AI-led work still accounts for less than 5% of total revenue, per UnearthInsight. Nomura's counterpoint: while AI is a deflationary force, "the same is being offset by incremental work and broader scope."

Mid-Caps to Buck the Trend

The divide between tier-1 and mid-tier firms keeps widening. Kotak forecasts quarter-on-quarter constant-currency growth of 7% for Persistent Systems, 4.5% for Coforge and 3.5% for Mphasis — against 0.5% for TCS, 1.1% for Infosys and 1.6% for Tech Mahindra. HDFC Securities puts tier-1 growth between -0.4% and 2%, versus 0.6% to 6.3% for the mid-tiers.

Broker stock picks reflect the split: Nomura has buys on Infosys and Cognizant among large caps and Coforge in mid-caps, while Choice Broking prefers TCS, Tech Mahindra and Mphasis.

One cushion for margins: the rupee's depreciation — 0.8% quarter-on-quarter and 8.4% year-on-year — has partly offset pricing pressure, and Kotak expects large-cap margins to be stable to marginally down year-on-year. Accenture's September 30 results offered a mixed read: improving AI demand signals, but conversion into revenue remains the metric to watch.

What Comes Next

TCS reports first, setting the tone for the season, with Infosys' October 22-23 board meeting the main event — guidance revision, deal commentary and any sign that AI deflation is stabilising will decide whether the sector's selloff finds a floor.

Diaspora Angle

AI deflation is now a hard number reshaping India's $283 billion IT sector — the employer of millions of Indian technology professionals at home and in the United States. The structural shift from headcount growth to AI-led delivery is exactly the transition playing out in the careers of diaspora engineers, and the mid-cap outperformers are where much of the hiring momentum has moved.
